pulls.title: 8397766: jdk/jfr/api/consumer/streaming/TestLatestEvent.java fails with Recording file is stuck in locked stream state
pulls.author: egahlin
pulls.body_excerpt: Could I have a review of a PR that fixes a problem where two chunks may get the same timestamp? The current code waits for a unique timestamp T before rotation, but before setOutput is invoked, time advances to T + 1, which is never stored. When the next rotation happens, it checks T against T + 1, which passes, so the next chunk may also get the T + 1 timestamp. The fix is to store the actual timestamp (e.g. T + 1) after rotation. When two chunks get the same timestamp, events/chunks may be missed, which leads to a timeout and test failure in this case. Testing: jdk/jdk/jfr + 100 * jdk/jdk/jf

pulls.author: suchismith1993
pulls.body_excerpt: JBS Issue : [JDK-8396867](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8396867) The ZGC pointer-atomic instructions (zCompareAndSwapP, zCompareAndSwapP_acq, zCompareAndExchangeP, zCompareAndExchangeP_acq, zGetAndSetP) declared their memory operand as iRegPdst, a register operand with only REG_INTER. pulls.title: 8397415: Splash JPEG decoder may retain freed frame storage after an allocation failure
pulls.author: Sovtouch
pulls.body_excerpt: SplashDecodeJpeg() allocates bitmap storage using stride * height as a signed int expression. SAFE_TO_ALLOC checks an unsigned 32-bit bound, so it can accept a mathematical product above INT_MAX. The allocation expression then has signed overflow and undefined behavior. If bitmap allocation fails, the function frees splash->frames but leaves its pointer and frameCount unchanged. The buffer-allocation failure path has the same ownership problem. A subsequent SplashCleanup(), including cleanup after an unsuccessful startup splash decode, can read freed frame storage and attempt to free it again.

pulls.body_excerpt: The goal of this PR is to avoid the saving and restoring of APX EGPRs around C2 calls to x86-64 stubs. pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, please consider. The current RVV element_compare uses a single-LMUL loop for all input sizes. Since short strings dominate in practice [1], the per-iteration loop overhead is disproportionate for small inputs. pulls.title: 8374307: Fix deoptimization storm caused by Action_none in GraphKit::uncommon_trap
pulls.author: bulasevich
pulls.body_excerpt: We observed a deoptimization storm caused by GraphKit::uncommon_trap generator logic. GraphKit::uncommon_trap considers the too_many_recompiles metric. If the threshold is overflowed, it replaces Deoptimization::Action_reinterpret with Deoptimization::Action_none (see code snippet below). This replacement changes the uncommon_trap logic: once execution hits a trap, the VM performs deoptimization but does not recompile the method anymore. In an "unlucky" case, when the code part calling this uncommon_trap becomes frequent, a deoptimization storm occurs (thousands of deoptimizations per second)
